# VULCAN Maintenance Report

## 1. DIAGNOSIS

Failure mode confirmed: **gear_tooth_fatigue_crack** [1]. Chip-detector / spall debris pattern is consistent with tooth-root fracture from a prior high-torque cobble event [4]. Oil viscosity sensor JSR.HR.STD1.GBX01.OIL.VISC reads **216.601 cSt — in WARNING band** (warn threshold 180, alarm 265) [2], indicating early oil degradation consistent with contamination from chunky spall debris [1].

> ⚠️ **Note on ML classifier:** The ML fault classifier currently returns NORMAL (P=0.9999) [2]. This is overridden by physical evidence (spall debris, fatigue crack morphology) and the elevated risk score [5]. Do not use ML confidence to defer action on this asset.

---

## 2. ROOT CAUSE

Tooth-root fatigue crack initiated by a prior **high-torque cobble event** — transient overload exceeding rated torque propagated a fatigue crack at the tooth root [4]. Chunky spall debris is now circulating in the oil circuit [1]. Per recurrence-prevention guidance, cobble events are the primary tooth fatigue initiator on this gearbox [9].

---

## 3. REMAINING USEFUL LIFE

| Parameter | Value |

| Estimated RUL | **632 cycles (~26.3 days)** [3] |
| RUL Band | Monitor [3] |
| Anomaly Score | 0.4898 (below anomaly threshold) [3] |

**Interpretation:** RUL model projects ~26 days, but physical crack evidence renders this estimate unreliable for deferral decisions. This is a **no-deferral** scenario — SOP explicitly states: *"gear tooth fatigue (SCN-038) is an immediate-stop event — no deferral permitted once chip detector alarms or spall is confirmed"* [8].

---

## 4. RISK CLASSIFICATION

**Overall Risk: HIGH — Score 7/10** [5]

| Factor | Contribution |

The 36-week lead time on the critical gear wheel is the dominant risk amplifier [5][6]. Every day of deferral increases exposure to catastrophic fracture during operation.

---

## 5. RECOMMENDED ACTIONS

Execute **SOP-02 Option B — Major Overhaul** [8]. Steps in strict sequence:

1. **Immediate controlled stop — no deferral** [4][6]
2. Remove gearbox via crane to repair bay [4][6]
3. Inspect all gear teeth under workshop lighting; classify damage per AGMA 2101-D04 (pitting / spalling / tooth-root fracture) [10]
4. Remove damaged gear wheel using hydraulic press; if shrink-fit, apply localised induction heat to gear boss only — no direct flame (annealing risk) [10]
5. Inspect gear seat on shaft for fretting/wear; measure against OEM tolerance — machine regrind + chrome-spray if worn [10]
6. Install new gear wheel + replace bearings as opportunity (bearing replacement cost is negligible vs. gearbox removal labour) [11]
7. Set backlash to **0.1–0.3 mm** — verify with dial gauge at minimum 8 tooth positions around circumference [11]
8. Check contact pattern with Prussian blue: must cover **>70% face width and >60% tooth height** [11]
9. Run-in at **low load before full torque** — do not return directly to full mill drive load [4][6]

---

|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ORDER NOW** | GEAR-WHL-M20 | Custom large-module gear wheel M20+ (HSM mill drive) | **Out of stock** | **36 weeks** — Flender / Renk OEM [6] |

- **Monthly ferrographic oil analysis** — detects gear spall particles 2–4 weeks before GMF alarm escalates to emergency stop [9]
- Implement continuous kidney-loop filtration; target **ISO 4406 < 16/14/11** [9]
- Connect torque measurement to CMMS; auto-raise work order if torque exceeds **110% rated for > 5 seconds** to catch cobble events before they propagate tooth cracks [9]
